premise: Midday on the Moon, sunlight everywhere — and the sky is black and full of stars; the whole base stops to look up.
inspiration: Andersen's 'What the Moon Saw' (the Moon telling what it sees), turned: what the Moon sees in its own sky.
lesson: The world is stranger and more wonderful than you expect.
learning: The Moon's sky is black even at noon: there is no air to light it up blue.

en-US.title: Black Sky at Noon
en-US.text: {canvas:daybreak 10s} [softly] Midday on the Moon. {all:glow 0.4} The Sun blazed down, bright and white. {canvas:glints 12s} The dust sparkled. Every rock threw a shadow as black as ink. {all:face happy} And then somebody looked up. {all:face surprised} [gasps] The sky was black. Pitch black, and full of stars, {all:hop} right in the middle of the day. {all:pulse} On Earth, the air scatters sunlight all over the sky and paints it blue. The Moon has no air at all. So here the sky stays dark, even at noon, {all:glow} and the stars never go away. {all:wobble} Everyone at the base stopped to look. [whispers] Sunshine on the ground. {all:sparkle} Stars overhead. {all:face happy} {all:hearts} [happily] Other places get a blue sky. The Moon gets both.

es-ES.title: Cielo negro al mediodía
es-ES.text: {canvas:daybreak 10s} [softly] Mediodía en la Luna. {all:glow 0.4} El Sol pegaba fuerte, blanco y brillante. {canvas:glints 12s} El polvo destellaba. Cada roca dejaba una sombra negra como la tinta. {all:face happy} Y entonces alguien miró arriba. {all:face surprised} [gasps] El cielo era negro. Negro, negrísimo, y lleno de estrellas, {all:hop} en pleno día. {all:pulse} En la Tierra, el aire reparte la luz del sol por todo el cielo y lo pinta de azul. La Luna no tiene nada de aire. Así que aquí el cielo se queda oscuro, incluso a mediodía, {all:glow} y las estrellas nunca se van. {all:wobble} Todos en la base se pararon a mirar. [whispers] Sol en el suelo. {all:sparkle} Estrellas en el cielo. {all:face happy} {all:hearts} [happily] Otros sitios tienen un cielo azul. La Luna tiene las dos cosas.
